title: Spin-charge separation in the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model
authors: Yuntian Gu, Hui Yang, Zhehao Dai, Yantao Wu
abstract: Recent experiments in moiré materials have enabled the realization of a variety of exotic quantum phases. In this context, the Hofstadter-Hubbard model has been proposed as a possible setting for hosting chiral spin liquid. Concurrently, significant progress has been recently made in the computational methods for two-dimensional many-body fermion systems, which makes numerically studying this challenging model a real possibility in genuine 2D geometry. Motivated by these advances, we investigate the putative chiral spin liquid phase in the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model using variational Monte Carlo with neural quantum states (NQS) and projected entangled pair states (PEPS). We observe spin-charge separation directly in real space through numerical spin-pumping simulation and real-time spin and charge motion. In addition, in the context of anyonic superconductivity conjectured in this model, we find a positive two-electron binding energy on small systems, but it decreases below our numerical resolution as the system size increases. Our work demonstrates NQS and PEPS as powerful tools, capable of cross-checking each other, for diagnosing topological order and fractionalized excitations in strongly correlated electronic systems.
summary: The paper investigates the chiral spin liquid phase in the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model using advanced quantum simulation methods. The authors demonstrate spin-charge separation by showing distinct real-space dynamics for spin and charge excitations. This work confirms the utility of NQS and PEPS as powerful tools for diagnosing topological order in strongly correlated electronic systems.
main_problem: The study investigates spin-charge separation (fractionalization) within the context of a putative chiral spin liquid phase.
main_result: The authors provide direct real-space evidence for spin-charge separation by observing that spin density localizes on the edge while excess charge diffuses into the bulk during time evolution simulations.
method: The research employs advanced quantum many-body techniques, specifically Variational Monte Carlo with Neural Quantum States (NQS) and Projected Entangled Pair States (PEPS), alongside real-time dynamics simulations.
model_or_system: The model is the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model, which is relevant to moiré materials and hosts potential chiral spin liquid phases. The Hamiltonian includes hopping terms modulated by a magnetic flux ($\Phi = \pi/2$ per triangle) and an onsite Hubbard interaction ($U$).
key_observables: Spin Hall response ($\sigma^s_{xy}$), Charge Hall response ($\sigma_{xy}$), real-space spin density vs. charge density evolution, and two-electron binding energy.
important_parameters: The key parameters are the hopping amplitude ($t$), the onsite interaction strength ($U$), and the magnetic flux $\Phi$. The analysis focuses on regimes around $U \approx 11$ where a transition to CSL is expected.
main_assumptions: The study assumes that NQS and PEPS can accurately diagnose topological order, although pairing evidence diminishes rapidly with system size, limiting conclusions about superconductivity in the thermodynamic limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate gap closing/opening as a function of $U$ (Fig. 2(b)), show direct real-space separation of spin and charge densities (Fig. 2(c,d) & Fig. 4), and demonstrate quantized spin pumping response upon flux insertion (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and methods, then analyzes gap behavior across different coupling regimes ($U$). It proceeds to provide direct evidence for SCS via real-space simulations and quantifies topological properties using charge/spin pumping measurements.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it uses sophisticated numerical techniques (NQS/PEPS) to probe fractionalized excitations, a core topic in strongly correlated physics that often connects to emergent phenomena studied in AMO systems like Rydberg arrays or cold atom lattices.

FIG. 4. Real-time PEPS dynamics of an injected electron in the CSL phase at U = 13 on a 6 × 6 cluster. The initial state contains one additional electron pinned near the upper-left corner by spin-dependent local attractive potentials h↑ pin = 4.4 and h↓ pin = 3.6. After the potential is removed at t = 0, the excess charge rapidly spreads into the bulk, while the spin density remains near the boundary and propagates along the edge. The contrasting charge and spin motion provides a direct dynamical signature of spin-charge separation.
